name: Back-up copy, failover and availability-after-cessation mechanisms
scope_note: Covers every concrete mechanism found for the ESPR back-up copy (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(4), Art. 27(1)(c), Art. 29(2)(c), Annex III point (l)) and for availability after insolvency, liquidation or cessation (ESPR Art. 11(e); Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 78(e)): the five CIRPASS-2 redirection options, the CIRPASS D3.2 root/default EU resolver and archive flow (HTTP and DID variants), the CIRPASS-2 D4.1 V1.1 recommendations 3.15 to 3.17 and building blocks, the GS1 in Europe failover proposals, the GS1 Web Vocabulary link types, the Catena-X backupReference field, the CIRPASS-2 mock-eu-registry liveURL/backupURL fields and code path, the BatteryPass-Ready Backup and Deletion modules, the official registry back-up link check (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(7)(e), Art. 8(9)(c), recital 16) as seen in the registry user guide v1.03, and the status of the DPP service-provider delegated act (Have Your Say initiative 14382). For each mechanism it states what a black-box tester can observe and over what time. It leaves out: the content of any EN, ISO, IEC or DIN document (bibliographic only); the registry XML/JSON upload templates and the registry test environment (behind EU Login, not contacted); vendor back-up products (no technical documentation located); DLT anchoring as an availability means (covered by sibling record m06); and CX-0160 bridging (sibling record m04, not re-read).
summary: EU law creates two related duties but no interface. Under the ESPR, the economic operator must make a back-up copy of the passport available through a DPP service provider when the product is placed on the market, and that copy must be of the most up-to-date version; the passport may name the provider that hosts the back-up (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(4), Art. 27(1)(c), Art. 29(2)(c), Annex III point (l)). Separately, passports must stay available for the period set in delegated acts, also after insolvency, liquidation or cessation of the responsible operator in the Union (ESPR Art. 11(e)); the Batteries Regulation has the same continuity rule (Art. 78(e)) but no back-up-copy duty. The registry implementing act lets the Commission check, where relevant, the link to the back-up held by a service provider, and lets the registry store a service-provider reference (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(7)(e), Art. 8(9)(c), recital 16). The live registry user guide v1.03 shows only UPI, model and batch identifiers for item-level battery registrations, so the back-up link check is not visible in practice today (inference, not a stated fact). How a user actually reaches the back-up when the primary host is gone is not fixed by any adopted law or open standard. The CIRPASS-2 report lists five options: a registry of primary and back-up links plus fallback redirection apps run by the Commission or others (option 1, favoured by most contributors), an EU-run domain with per-operator subdomains and DNS re-pointing (option 2), a central EU redirect for every UPI (option 3), seizure of lapsed domains by an EU agency (option 4), and a second, mechanically derived EU URL used by machines (option 5). CIRPASS D3.2 proposes an EU root or default resolver, fed by the registry, that a DPP-aware app asks after a 'host not found' or HTTP 404, and a DID variant where the DID document carries a 'backup' service next to 'dpp'. CIRPASS-2 D4.1 V1.1 turns this into recommendations: operator-run UPI-to-URI redirection that survives insolvency (3.16), an EU fallback redirection service of last resort (3.17), and a back-up provider that holds all data, stays current and enforces the same access rules (3.15). GS1 in Europe proposes host substitution on a GS1 Digital Link URI (the domain is not part of the GS1 identifier) and the registry as lookup of last resort, possibly via a registry-signed DID listing primary and back-up endpoints. At the data-model level, Catena-X DPP 7.0.0 makes backupReference a required free-text field, while the CIRPASS-2 mock registry requires backupURL but fetches and hashes only liveURL. A black-box tester can therefore check presence, syntax, host independence, reachability and content equivalence of a declared back-up at a point in time, and failover behaviour only on loopback fixtures; lifetime availability cannot be proven by any finite number of observations.

maturity.spec_status: No adopted technical specification exists for back-up hosting, synchronisation or failover. Law (ESPR, Batteries, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778) states duties only. CIRPASS-2 material is project output: the redirection report is a collection of opinions, not a decision; D4.1 V1.1 is a set of non-normative recommendations whose pages carry a 'Draft' watermark. GS1 in Europe 5.3 is a position paper; GS1 standards define no back-up link type. Catena-X backupReference is a released (status 'release') SAMM property whose meaning is stated as to be defined later. The DPP service-provider delegated act is not adopted.

maturity.adoption_evidence: No production fallback redirection service, EU root resolver or EU back-up domain was located. The official registry is live for item-level battery registrations (user guide v1.03) and its documented form has no back-up field. Pilots and prototypes: CIRPASS-2 mock-eu-registry (backupURL field, not dereferenced); BatteryPass-Ready user stories v1.0 model a Backup Service Provider with Backup and Deletion modules; Made2Verify (Procedia Computer Science 277, 2026) reports a GS1-based resolver with a fallback dashboard tested on one remanufactured part (abstract only). Stakeholder preferences (not law, not oracle): the service-provider consultation had 275 valid responses (8 April to 1 July 2025); most respondents chose 99 % yearly availability as the minimum acceptable level; of 92 prospective providers, 71 (77.2 %) intend failover clustering, 80 (87 %) redundant servers, 86 (93.5 %) monitoring and alerts (factual summary report Ares(2025)6861790). The call for evidence lists 'providing backup tools and services' as one of eight provider activities in scope.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: ESPR: back-up copy through a DPP service provider at placing on the market (Art. 10(4)); manufacturers and importers ensure the passport is available including a back-up copy of the most up-to-date version stored by a provider (Art. 27(1)(c), Art. 29(2)(c)); Annex III point (l) lists the reference of the provider hosting the back-up as possible passport content; storage by the operator or by providers (Art. 11(c)); availability for the delegated-act period also after insolvency, liquidation or cessation of activity in the Union (Art. 11(e)); providers may not sell or reuse data beyond the service (Art. 11, second subparagraph); requirements and a possible certification scheme for providers by delegated act (Art. 11, third subparagraph; not adopted). Batteries: storage by the responsible operator or authorised operators (Art. 78(c)), no reuse (Art. 78(d)), availability after the responsible operator ceases to exist or to operate in the Union (Art. 78(e)); no back-up-copy duty in Art. 77 or 78. Registry: Commission checks the back-up link where relevant (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(7)(e), recital 16), stores a service-provider reference where relevant (Art. 8(9)(c)), keeps a list of verified service providers (Art. 3(f), recital 3), allows transfer of registered passports to another verified actor including after cessation (Art. 6a, recital 10), deletes registration data 10 years after registration unless Union law sets another period (Art. 10(3)), and is available at all times except announced maintenance (Art. 15(2)).

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Failover depends on separating the identifier from the host. GS1 Digital Link: the GS1 keys sit in the path (/01/{GTIN}/10/{lot}/21/{serial}); the domain is not part of the GS1 identifier and the same keys may appear under several domains; a canonical form uses https://id.gs1.org (URI Syntax 1.7.0, sections 2, 4.11, 4.12, 5). GS1 in Europe 5.3 builds on this: a client that fails on https://brand.example/01/09506000164908 can substitute another known host. CIRPASS-2 D4.1 'Fallback Product UPI to URL' block gives two input shapes: an opaque UPI passed as a query (example https://upi-uri-service.example?upi=ABC1234) and a GS1 Digital Link where only the host is replaced. CIRPASS-2 option 5 derives a second URL mechanically (qr.example.com/identifier -> qr.example.com.dpp.eu/identifier). D3.2 DID variant: the identifier is a DID URL carrying the service selector, e.g. did:example:123456789abcdefghi?service=dpp, with a 'backup' service as alternative. Registry: the UPI is a mandatory HTTPS URL of at most 2000 characters (user guide v1.03).

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: From one sample artifact: whether the carrier URI parses into host plus GS1 keys (identifier.parse today covers /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial> only); whether the same keys resolve under an alternative host (loopback only). From a DID URL: presence of a backup service selector. Single-shot observation suffices for syntax; nothing about persistence follows from it.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: ESPR Art. 2(30) requires that the UPI enables a web link; it does not require host independence or a second resolvable form. Host substitution and DID backup selectors are proposals.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: Mechanisms that put an EU-owned domain or a second URL into the carrier (options 2, 3, 5) lengthen the encoded string; contributors note larger QR codes and more NFC memory and a region-specific label (report sections 2.2 and 2.3). Option 1 and GS1 host substitution leave the carrier unchanged. D3.2 DID variant puts the DID URL, including the service parameter, in the carrier.

specs.component: 4.2 DID data flows (carrier holds DID URL with service IDs)

L02_data_carriers.observable_black_box: Decoded payload of a sample carrier image (carrier.qr_decode): which host is encoded, its length, and whether a DID URL with a backup selector is present. Static; one observation.
L02_data_carriers.law_delta: Carrier rules come from Art. 10(1) and delegated acts; no adopted act requires a fallback-ready carrier content.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: (1) Client-side fallback after failure: D3.2 defines the trigger as DNS 'host not found' or HTTP 404 from the REO resolver or repository; the app then asks a hard-coded default EU root resolver, which either returns the DPP location or redirects to another resolver (D3.2 3.1.10, 3.1.13.2, 4.1). DID variant: on 404 from the 'dpp' service endpoint, the app sends GET to the 'backup' endpoint listed in the DID document (D3.2 4.2.2.2). (2) Redirection semantics: D4.1 'Redirection' block allows either a transparent proxy or HTTP 3xx with a Location header, possibly a list of locations; the redirection report defines a web redirection service by reference to RFC 9110 redirection (input one URI, output one or more URIs) and a DNS redirection service (resolution of a subdomain changed by its owner). (3) Option 2: EU DNS service maps <operator>.dpp.eu by CNAME to the operator host and re-points it to a back-up host on cessation; DNS propagation delays failover. (4) Option 3: every carrier URI is www.DPPlinkregistry.eu/<UPI>; the central service redirects to the active or back-up link after being told of cessation and would need to crawl to detect undeclared failures. (5) Resolver federation: GS1-conformant resolvers can hand a request to another resolver; the GS1 link type 'handledBy' (restricted to resolvers) marks such delegation. No GS1 link type for a back-up, archive or mirror exists among the 60 keys read. (6) Web app: GS1 in Europe 5.3 suggests a registry- or provider-hosted web app (with scanner) that detects a failed fetch and tells the user it will redirect to the back-up. (7) Registry dereferencing: the official registry fetches the UPI at registration and rejects excessive redirects, redirects to a less secure protocol, disallowed domains or ports and oversized responses (user guide 6, 'Registration Validation Errors').

L03_data_exchange_protocols.observable_black_box: With loopback fixtures: status codes and Location chain from the primary; behaviour of the declared fallback service when the primary fixture returns 404, 410, 5xx, refuses connections or has no DNS entry; whether the fallback returns the back-up location (single shot per fault). Redirect chain length and scheme downgrade (single shot). DNS re-pointing and propagation delay are observable only over hours and only with a controlled DNS fixture, which the engine does not have. Against a live SUT a tester can see the current redirect target, but cannot induce a real cessation.
L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: No adopted law or open standard fixes the fallback route, the trigger (404 versus 410 versus DNS failure) or the response format of a fallback service; D4.1 3.17 asks the Commission to define infrastructure, governance and APIs.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: D4.1 places 'Ensure DPP portability (backup, transfer)' in its Lifecycle API block: a portability call takes DPP data and information about the target data sink and returns a status code or result message plus a link to the back-up for back-up operations; the 'Back-up' block stores and accepts updates independently of the responsible operator and returns the location of the back-up; the 'DPP portability' block transfers data for back-up and for change of provider. D4.1 recommends JSON-LD as the default exchange format and says its lifecycle API should follow the CEN-CENELEC JTC 24 specification (named only; content not used). The 'Notification' block can tell a provider to start serving the back-up as the active DPP, e.g. on insolvency, with handler pull or repository push. BatteryPass-Ready v1.0 methodology: a Backup module creates or updates the back-up copy at the Backup Service Provider after each registration or update; a Deletion module removes public hosting, soft-deletes at the provider and notifies the registry. CIRPASS-2 mock registry API: POST /metadata/v1 with JSON including liveURL and backupURL; GET /metadata/v1/{registryId}/proof returns a signed JWT with dppHash and dppContentType.

specs.component: building blocks Lifecycle API, Back-up, DPP portability, Notification

mock-eu-registry README and DPPMetadataService.java (proof JWT claims)

variants: continuous or one-off transfer before closing (D3.2 table step 1)
L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.observable_black_box: Only through an operator-facing API, which a passive tester normally lacks: after a declared update at the primary, the time until the back-up shows the same version (needs repeated polling; minutes to days); whether a deactivated passport is soft-deleted at the back-up. Without write access a tester sees only the two read endpoints.
L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.law_delta: Law requires the back-up to hold the most up-to-date version (ESPR Art. 27(1)(c), 29(2)(c)) but sets no synchronisation interval, API or notification; all API shapes here are project proposals.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Catena-X DPP 7.0.0: MetadataEntity property backupReference (samm-c:Text, example 'https://dummy.link'), listed without samm:optional, and in the generated JSON schema it is in 'required' of MetadataCharacteristic with version, expirationDate, issueDate, passportIdentifier, predecessor, language, economicOperator; its description cites ESPR Annex III (l), Art. 10(4), Art. 27 and 29(c) and says the attribute 'will be further defined in the future'. Catena-X battery_pass 6.1.0 has no backup property. CIRPASS-2 mock registry schema: backupURL required, type string, format uri, pattern ^http, example https://backup-dpp.example.com/product/12345, beside liveURL with the same constraints. D4.1 recommends JSON-LD as default exchange format for back-up and portability. GS1 in Europe suggests a registry-signed DID document listing primary and back-up DPP URLs as service endpoints.

specs.component: Back-up and DPP portability blocks ('Standardize the default exchange format as JSON-LD')

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.observable_black_box: From one passport payload: presence of a back-up reference field, its type (URL versus name), and whether it parses as an absolute HTTPS URL; whether it differs in host from the primary. From a registry record (mock): presence and syntax of backupURL. Single observation.
L05_system_interoperability_data_models.law_delta: Annex III (l) asks for a 'reference of the provider', not a URL; Catena-X models it as free text and makes it required, the mock registry as a URL. No adopted delegated act fixes the field yet.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Hosting: primary at the operator or a provider (ESPR Art. 11(c); Batteries Art. 78(c)); back-up copy at a provider (ESPR Art. 10(4)), of the most up-to-date version (Art. 27(1)(c), 29(2)(c)). GS1 in Europe treats it as self-evident that the back-up must be independent of every part of the primary system. D4.1 3.15: the back-up provider stores all data including optional data, keeps it current, enforces the same access rules; its contents must be complete when the DPP is created and registered. D3.2 3.1.13 separates operational back-up (normal hosting practice, not a second structure) from an archive of last resort that may answer slowly and, for long-term archives, may hold only the strictly necessary data; D3.2 table (5.2) sketches cessation: (1) operator transfers all data to a back-up provider, optionally continuously; (2) the provider takes over the domain name, or on 404 a prefix transforms the URI into the archive's resolver; (3) the provider restores all data or only the mandatory subset, with a possible 'ultimate' back-up if the provider also fails; (4) the provider activates the domain with links to the data. D3.2 states that the back-up/archive flow was not described in its architectures and must be addressed later. Option 4 has an EU agency take over lapsed domain names. Cobuilder notes that for construction products the back-up provider would serve the passport as the only source from 10 to 25 years after market withdrawal. Registry retention: registration data deleted 10 years after registration unless Union law sets another period (2026/1778 Art. 10(3)).

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.observable_black_box: Point in time: back-up location declared; reachable; same host or same provider as the primary (DNS name, certificate subject, IP range as heuristics only); content equal to the primary as canonical JSON or digest; same restricted fields hidden. Over time (persistence.scheduled, interface_only): periodic paired fetches of primary and back-up show drift and the lag after a primary version change; a run over weeks shows uptime against a declared target. A finite run cannot prove availability for the delegated-act period or after a real cessation.
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.law_delta: Law fixes the duty and the continuity goal. It does not fix independence of the back-up provider from the primary host, the synchronisation interval, the availability level, the archive form, or what happens if the back-up provider also fails. Batteries have no back-up-copy duty, only Art. 78(e) continuity.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: D4.1 3.15 and its access-control section: the back-up must apply the same access control as the responsible operator, at least for mandatory data, so access management must be transferable to the back-up provider; whether operator-specific extra roles transfer is left to contracts. D4.1 notes that the ESPR requires authenticity to stay verifiable when data come from a back-up, cache or successor host (its reading of Art. 11(g)), and recommends signed DPP records. Redirection report: options 2 and 3 raise denial-of-service, subdomain-takeover (ExtraRed) and scan-surveillance concerns (GS1, IOXIO, TNO). D3.2: privileged requests carry credentials (e.g. JWT) to REST endpoints; nothing specific to the back-up.

specs.component: 3.15; DPP integrity rationale; access control requirements ('Exchangeable across organizations')

variants: mirrored access policy at the back-up
L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.observable_black_box: Anonymous request to the back-up must not expose fields hidden at the primary (single shot); role tokens accepted at the primary should be accepted at the back-up (needs test credentials for both). Takeover risk of a dangling CNAME is observable only with a DNS fixture.
L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.law_delta: Equal access control at the back-up is a CIRPASS-2 recommendation; law states access rights per delegated act and security in general terms (Art. 11(b), (h)).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Integrity of the copy: the mock registry stores 'sha256' of the body fetched from liveURL (dpp_hash VARCHAR(71)) and its Content-Type, and puts dppHash and dppContentType in a proof-of-registration JWT signed with the registry RSA key per the README (algorithm identifier not read; issuer and key id configured; JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json); it never fetches backupURL. Official registry stores the passport integrity as evidence of registration (2026/1778 Art. 8(9)(d)). D4.1: original DPP and each update signed by the issuer so that a copy served by a provider or successor stays verifiable; on succession the outgoing operator signs a succession statement with the successor identifier, effective date and qualified timestamp; if it is insolvent, the back-up provider attests the successor based on verifiable legal evidence; historical records stay valid. GS1 in Europe 5.3 way 1: a registry-signed DID listing primary and back-up endpoints.

specs.component: mock-eu-registry DPPMetadataService.generateHashAndApplyValidations, getDpp, asJWT; README v1.0.0 to v1.1.0 migration
DPP integrity rationale; recommendation on update hash chain and succession; 3.15 implementation guidance

variants: registry-held digest of the live copy
issuer-signed DPP verifiable at any host
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: Digest of the back-up body versus the digest in a registry proof or the primary (single shot); signature on the back-up copy verifies against the issuer key (integrity.jws for JWS); signed succession statement present after a handover (needs a fixture).
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: ESPR Art. 11(g) requires authentication, reliability and integrity in general; no rule says the back-up must be signed or that the registry hash covers it.

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: Law: the Commission checks, where relevant, the link to the back-up hosted by a DPP service provider at registration, together with structure, granularity and commodity code; the check does not prove compliance (2026/1778 Art. 8(7)(e), recital 16); the registry stores a provider reference where relevant (Art. 8(9)(c)) and a list of verified providers (Art. 3(f)). Practice: the user guide v1.03 form takes UPI (mandatory HTTPS URL, max 2000 characters), optional model and batch identifiers, item level only for batteries; uploads of up to 100 records as XML or JSON; no back-up field is described and the error list has no back-up error; the registry dereferences the UPI and fails on redirect loops, scheme downgrade, disallowed domains or ports. The guide says the registry records 'the location where the passport is hosted' and that the operator keeps the DPP 'resolvable at all times'. Proposals: registry as holder of primary and back-up links for fallback apps (option 1; EON example primary matts-company.com/api/dpp/{id}, backup eon.xyz/dpp-backup/api/dpp/{id}); D4.1 registry block registers DPP location and back-up location if the Commission builds the fallback service; D3.2 registry as 'resolver of resolvers' updated with the new current (back-up) resolver through the same API; GS1 in Europe: registry as lookup of last resort (dpp.eu suggested) with three ways: links to original and back-up, ordered list of certified providers, or a registry-held copy on request. Mock registry: backupURL required, schema-validated only.

specs.component: chapter 6 DPP Registration; Registration Validation Errors

variants: registry lists certified providers to try in order (GS1 in Europe way 2)
registry keeps a copy (GS1 in Europe way 3, not envisaged by ESPR)
L09_registry_and_customs.observable_black_box: Against the engine mock registry: presence and syntax of a back-up field, host independence from the live URL, reachability and equivalence of the back-up. The official registry and its test environment are not callable by the engine (registry.official interface_only). From the passport: a back-up provider reference that should match the registry record. Single shot.
L09_registry_and_customs.law_delta: The check of the back-up link is 'where relevant' and its method is not described; the live guide shows no back-up input. Using the registry as a fallback resolver is not in any adopted act.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Transfer and succession: 2026/1778 Art. 6a allows transfer of registered passports to another verified operator or value-chain actor from a stated date, including after cessation (recital 10); verified status lapses after three years or at expiry of the eID means (Art. 4(4), 5(4)). D4.1: succession statement signed by the outgoing operator, or an attestation by the back-up provider if the operator is insolvent; the redirection service is then re-pointed to the successor; user stories 10 (change provider), 11 (become new rEO), 12 (provider makes back-up available when the rEO stops), 13 (stop hosting after expected lifetime). Registry versions every change with a Commission timestamp (Art. 10(1)-(2)). BatteryPass-Ready: Backup module after each update; Deletion soft-deletes at the back-up provider. Catena-X: predecessor and backupReference sit together in metadata.

specs.component: user stories table (6, 10-13); succession guidance; 3.16 implementation guidance

variants: back-up becomes the active passport without a successor
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.observable_black_box: Over repeated observations: version at the primary versus the back-up; after a simulated hand-over (fixture), the redirect target changes and a signed succession record appears; old signed versions still verify. persistence.versions covers version order on one host only.
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.law_delta: Law gives the transfer mechanism in the registry (Art. 6a) but no rule for activating the back-up as the active passport or for who updates it after cessation.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Roles: DPP service provider is an independent third party authorised by the operator (ESPR Art. 2(32)); not an economic operator; requirements and a possible certification scheme await the delegated act (Art. 11, third subparagraph). Initiative 14382 (PLAN/2024/1820): call for evidence Ares(2024)8031852 of 12/11/2024 (178 feedback items; indicative Q1-Q2 2026; scope includes 'providing backup tools and services'; requirements on information security and financial viability for long-term access; options self-declaration, enforcement or ex ante certification); public consultation 8 April to 1 July 2025 (275 valid responses; summary Ares(2025)6861790 dated 25/08/2025); draft act not published; planned adoption Q4 2026 per the Have Your Say API. Fallback governance proposals: Commission alone or with sector associations and producer responsibility organisations (option 1); Commission DNS registry (option 2); Commission central redirector (option 3); EU agency taking over domains (option 4); D4.1 3.16 catalogue of redirection services and portability between them; D3.2 sector-wide fallback resolvers financed like insurance by branch members.

specs.component: Art. 2(32), Art. 11 second and third subparagraphs

L11_roles_and_governance.observable_black_box: Who operates the primary and back-up hosts (domain owner, certificate subject: heuristics); whether the back-up provider appears in the registry list of verified providers (not callable by the engine). Contracts, certification and financial viability are not observable; record them as manual evidence.
L11_roles_and_governance.law_delta: Who operates a fallback redirection service, and who activates the back-up after cessation, is undecided; the service-provider delegated act is not adopted.

end_to_end_flows.name: Option 1: registry of primary and back-up links plus fallback redirection app (CIRPASS-2 report; D4.1 3.17)
actors: operator redirection service and primary repository
fallback redirection service (Commission, sector association, PRO, or provider)
steps: 1. The operator registers the UPI with the primary DPP location and the back-up location (EON example: primary matts-company.com/api/dpp/{id}, back-up eon.xyz/dpp-backup/api/dpp/{id}).
2. Normal use: the carrier URL (e.g. matts-company.com/id/123456) resolves at the operator; the registry is not involved.
3. The primary fails or the operator ceases activity; a generic browser sees a dead link (no automatic redirect).
4. A DPP-aware app or the Commission web app looks up the UPI in the registry and calls the back-up source; machine clients are reprogrammed to use the fallback service.

end_to_end_flows.name: D3.2 HTTP: default EU (root) resolver after host-not-found or 404
steps: 1. The app decodes the UPI URI and sends GET to the REO resolver.
2. The network layer returns 'host not found', or the repository returns HTTP 404.
3. The app asks the default EU resolver, hard-coded in the app and fed by registry data, which returns the archive or back-up location or redirects to a resolver that knows it.
4. The app fetches the archived passport; the archive may answer slowly and may hold reduced data.

end_to_end_flows.name: D3.2 DID: backup service endpoint in the product DID document
steps: 1. The carrier holds a DID URL with service=dpp (and a backup service ID).
2. The app resolves the DID document and sends GET without credentials to the dpp service endpoint.
3. On HTTP 404 the app sends GET to the backup service endpoint from the same DID document.
4. After cessation the DID document must be changed to point to the provider (D3.2 table step 2).

end_to_end_flows.name: D3.2 cessation hand-over table (not validated in D3.2)
steps: 1. Before closing, the operator transfers all DPP data to a back-up provider (optionally continuously).
2. The provider takes control of the operator's DPP domain name, or a standard prefix rewrites 404 URIs into the archive resolver.
3. The provider restores all data or only the mandatory subset.
4. The provider activates the domain with links to the data.

end_to_end_flows.name: Option 2 and option 3: EU-controlled names
steps: 1. Carrier encodes <operator>.dpp.eu/... (option 2) or www.DPPlinkregistry.eu/<UPI> (option 3).
2. Normal use: CNAME (option 2) or HTTP redirect (option 3) to the operator host.
3. After the Commission is told of cessation (or detects it by crawling, option 3), it re-points the name or the redirect to the back-up host.
4. Clients follow automatically; failover lags DNS propagation in option 2.

end_to_end_flows.name: GS1 in Europe: host substitution and registry of last resort
steps: 1. The web app scans the GS1 Digital Link carrier; resolution at the brand host fails.
2. The app parses the GS1 keys and retries with a known alternative host, or a federated resolver hands the request on (handledBy).
3. If no alternative is known, the app asks the registry, which returns the back-up link, a list of certified providers to try in order, or a copy on request.
4. The app tells the user it is now showing the back-up.

end_to_end_flows.name: BatteryPass-Ready modules: back-up after every write
steps: 1. Registration returns the registration ID.
2. Create DPP at the main service provider.
3. Backup module creates or updates the copy at the backup service provider; repeated after each update.
4. Deletion removes public hosting, soft-deletes at the backup provider and notifies the registry.

failure_modes.fault: Back-up URL equals the live URL or points at the same resolver (e.g. both at id.gs1.org/01/...).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare hosts and final targets of the two URLs.

failure_modes.fault: Back-up is stale: holds an older version or lacks optional data.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Digest and version comparison of paired fetches.

failure_modes.fault: Registry accepts a dead back-up link because only the live URL is dereferenced (as in mock-eu-registry 1.1.1).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Register a record whose backupURL answers 404 on a loopback fixture and observe acceptance.

failure_modes.fault: Back-up serves restricted fields publicly because access policy was not mirrored.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Anonymous request to the back-up compared with the primary.

failure_modes.fault: Provider re-signs or re-serialises the copy so the issuer signature no longer verifies.
failure_modes.detectable_by: integrity.jws on the back-up copy against the issuer key.

failure_modes.fault: Fallback triggers only on 404 and not on DNS failure, connection refusal or 410/5xx.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Fault matrix on the switchable primary fixture.

failure_modes.fault: Redirect loop between fallback resolver and a dead primary, or scheme downgrade in the chain.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Redirect chain trace with a hop limit.

failure_modes.fault: backupReference holds a placeholder (e.g. 'https://dummy.link') or a provider name where a URL is expected.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Value rules: absolute HTTPS URL, not an example domain, resolvable on fixture.

failure_modes.fault: Dangling DNS name of a ceased operator taken over by a third party (option 2 subdomain or lapsed brand domain).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Not detectable without a DNS fixture; record as manual review.

failure_modes.fault: After operator cessation nobody can update the back-up, and no successor statement exists.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Absence of a succession record and stale lastModification over repeated observations.

failure_modes.fault: Passport names a back-up provider that differs from the one in the registry record.
failure_modes.detectable_by: registry.consistency extended to the back-up field.

open_questions: Do the official registry XML/JSON upload templates or the API carry a back-up link or provider-reference field? The user guide v1.03 form does not show one; the templates sit behind EU Login and were not retrieved.
How will the Commission perform the Art. 8(7)(e) back-up link check (syntax, dereference, comparison with the live copy)? Not described in the act or the guide.

Will the service-provider delegated act define a back-up interface, synchronisation interval, availability level or activation procedure after cessation? Planned adoption date differs by source (Q1-Q2 2026, Q4 2026, Q2/Q3 2027); no draft published.
Does any adopted or planned act create an EU fallback redirection service or root resolver (D4.1 3.17)? None located.

Batteries: is a back-up copy expected despite no duty in Regulation (EU) 2023/1542? BatteryPass-Ready assumes yes from Art. 78(e); the call for evidence links provider rules to batteries as the first product group.
Which trigger should a fallback client treat as cessation: DNS failure, connection refusal, 404, 410 or a signed tombstone? Sources differ (D3.2: host-not-found or 404).
Should the engine treat a back-up hosted by the same provider as the primary as a fail? Law does not say; GS1 in Europe and D4.1 lean to independence, D3.2 allows the same company.
Made2Verify: is there code or an API description for the fallback dashboard? Only the abstract was read.

CIRPASS-2 D4.1 V1.1 is the latest Zenodo version but every page carries a 'Draft' watermark.

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 8(7)(e) foresees a back-up link check, yet the registry user guide v1.03 shows no back-up input and no back-up error; this may be because the only live product group (batteries) has no ESPR back-up duty (inference).
BatteryPass-Ready v1.0 states that the registry entry foresees the identifier of the back-up operator; this matches Art. 8(9)(c) only as 'reference to the service provider, where relevant'.

Catena-X backupReference description says the attribute is mandatory and to be defined later, and the example value is a placeholder URL; the registrationIdentifier description still cites the January 2024 provisional ESPR text (Art. 12) rather than adopted Art. 13.
CIRPASS-2 mock-eu-registry requires backupURL but never dereferences it; a test that relies on the mock to validate back-ups would pass dead links.
